name: Carbon blacks or Vegetable carbon
unresolved_question: Does Schedule 8 title "Carbon blacks or Vegetable carbon" allow non-vegetable industrial carbon black, conflicting with plant-origin tile copy?

sources.what: Official Schedule 8 name is "Carbon blacks or Vegetable carbon" (153).
JECFA additive is "Vegetable Carbon"; synonyms include "Vegetable black" and "Carbon black (vegetable sources)"; produced by carbonising vegetable material.
FSANZ consumer materials refer to vegetable carbon (carbon black), INS 153, as the colour assessed/discussed.

verified_facts: AU Schedule 8 naming includes the synonym pair Carbon blacks / Vegetable carbon for code 153.
JECFA identity for INS 153 is vegetable carbon from vegetable sources, not furnace carbon black generally.
unsupported_possibilities: Treating Schedule 8 'Carbon blacks' as authorising petroleum/furnace carbon black unrelated to vegetable carbonisation.
notes: Existing tile/expanded correctly describe vegetable carbon. No copy change. Evidence fields untouched.

before.tile_summary: Vegetable carbon is an intensely black colouring made from carbon-rich plant material.
before.expanded_summary: Vegetable carbon is an intensely black colouring made from carbon-rich plant material. The material is carbonised and purified rather than used as ordinary charcoal.
before.fact_1_copy: Used for black or very dark colouring.
before.fact_2_copy: The carbon can originate from plant material even though the final ingredient is predominantly elemental carbon.

after.tile_summary: Vegetable carbon is an intensely black colouring made from carbon-rich plant material.
after.expanded_summary: Vegetable carbon is an intensely black colouring made from carbon-rich plant material. The material is carbonised and purified rather than used as ordinary charcoal.
after.fact_1_copy: Used for black or very dark colouring.
after.fact_2_copy: The carbon can originate from plant material even though the final ingredient is predominantly elemental carbon.

name: Sodium sulphite
unresolved_question: Can a sulphite-sensitivity / declaration cue be added with substance-family authority?

sources.what: Schedule 9 requires declaration of added sulphites at 10 mg/kg or more.
FSANZ states some sulphite-sensitive people may react; labelling at ≥10 mg/kg helps avoidance.

verified_facts: 221 is a sulphite salt in the preservative family.
AU/NZ mandatory sulphite declaration threshold is 10 mg/kg added sulphites.
unsupported_possibilities: Product-specific sensitivity diagnosis or prevalence claims.
notes: Added restrained label cue only; no medical overclaim.

before.tile_summary: Sodium sulphite is a sulphite salt used to preserve foods and control browning.
before.expanded_summary: Sodium sulphite is a sulphite salt used to preserve foods and control browning. In food it can release sulphur dioxide-related preserving species.
before.fact_1_copy: Part of the sulphite preservative family.
before.fact_2_copy: Used for preservation, antioxidant action and browning control.

after.tile_summary: Sodium sulphite is a sulphite salt used to preserve foods and control browning.
after.expanded_summary: Sodium sulphite is a sulphite salt used to preserve foods and control browning. In food it can release sulphur dioxide-related preserving species. In Australia and New Zealand, added sulphites at 10 mg/kg or more must be declared, which helps people who need to avoid sulphites.
after.fact_1_copy: Part of the sulphite preservative family.
after.fact_2_copy: Used for preservation, antioxidant action and browning control.
after.fact_3_copy: Added sulphites at 10 mg/kg or more must be declared on packaged foods in Australia and New Zealand.

before.tile_summary: Potassium sulphite is a salt in the sulphite family, used for preservation and antioxidant effects.

name: γ-Tocopherol
unresolved_question: Is 308 natural/plant-extracted gamma-tocopherol or synthetic gamma-tocopherol under FSANZ/JECFA?

sources.what: Schedule 15 lists 308 as Synthetic gamma-tocopherol (distinct from 307b Tocopherols concentrate, mixed).
JECFA mixed tocopherol concentrate is INS 307b (not 308).

verified_facts: FSANZ Schedule 15 identity for 308 is synthetic gamma-tocopherol.
307b is the mixed concentrate from vegetable-oil streams.
unsupported_possibilities: Leaving PLANT_EXTRACT profile unchanged as if it were authoritative identity (profile is now inconsistent with corrected editorial copy).
notes: Editorial fields corrected to synthetic listing. FOUNDER APPROVAL REQUIRED before changing source_preparation_profile from PLANT_EXTRACT to CHEMICAL_SYNTHESIS (governed source field).

before.tile_summary: Gamma-tocopherol is one of the naturally occurring tocopherols in the vitamin E family.
before.expanded_summary: Gamma-tocopherol is one of the naturally occurring tocopherols in the vitamin E family. It is fat-soluble and can help slow oxidation.
before.fact_1_copy: Found naturally in vegetable oils and other plant foods.
before.fact_2_copy: Used as an antioxidant in fat-containing foods.

after.tile_summary: Synthetic gamma-tocopherol is a manufactured form of one of the tocopherols in the vitamin E family.
after.expanded_summary: Synthetic gamma-tocopherol is a manufactured form of one of the tocopherols in the vitamin E family. In the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code it is listed as synthetic gamma-tocopherol (308), distinct from mixed tocopherols concentrate (307b). It is fat-soluble and is used as an antioxidant in fat-containing foods.
after.fact_1_copy: FSANZ Schedule 15 lists 308 as synthetic gamma-tocopherol, separate from mixed tocopherols concentrate (307b).
after.fact_2_copy: Used as an antioxidant in fat-containing foods.
after.fact_3_copy: The additive number alone does not mean the ingredient was extracted as a mixed natural tocopherol concentrate.

name: Potassium adipate
unresolved_question: May commercial potassium adipate be described as petrochemical-derived?

sources.what: Sibling entry e355 (adipic acid) already states petrochemical-derived intermediates in governed source_preparation_copy.

verified_facts: Potassium adipate is a salt of adipic acid.
e355 already carries a petrochemical manufacturing statement for adipic acid.
unsupported_possibilities: Asserting petrochemical origin on e357 without a substance-specific source_preparation statement on this entry.
notes: Do not invent petro claim on e357. Optional founder decision: align e357 SP with e355 parent-acid manufacturing note.

before.tile_summary: Potassium adipate is a potassium salt of adipic acid, a manufactured acid.
before.expanded_summary: Potassium adipate is a potassium salt of adipic acid, a manufactured acid with two acid groups (a dicarboxylic acid). It is used mainly for acidity control or related processing functions.
before.fact_2_copy: Used mainly for acidity control or related processing functions.

after.tile_summary: Potassium adipate is a potassium salt of adipic acid, a manufactured acid.
after.expanded_summary: Potassium adipate is a potassium salt of adipic acid, a manufactured acid with two acid groups (a dicarboxylic acid). It is used mainly for acidity control or related processing functions.

name: Ferric ammonium citrate
unresolved_question: What concrete food function does ferric ammonium citrate have?

sources.what: Functional uses: nutrient/dietary supplement (brown salt); nutrient/dietary supplement and anticaking agent for sodium chloride (green salt).

verified_facts: JECFA functional uses include nutrient/dietary supplement and anticaking for salt.
unsupported_possibilities: Claiming a single exclusive modern AU food use without Schedule 15 context.

before.tile_summary: Ferric ammonium citrate is an iron-containing citrate complex rather than a single simple salt.
before.expanded_summary: Ferric ammonium citrate is an iron-containing citrate complex rather than a single simple salt. It combines iron with citrate and ammonium in a water-compatible form.
before.fact_1_copy: A complex of iron with citrate and ammonium, not simply iron metal or plain citric acid.
before.fact_2_copy: Used where iron and citrate chemistry provides the desired technological effect.

after.tile_summary: Ferric ammonium citrate is an iron-containing citrate complex rather than a single simple salt.
after.expanded_summary: Ferric ammonium citrate is an iron-containing citrate complex rather than a single simple salt. It combines iron with citrate and ammonium in a water-compatible form. JECFA describes functional uses as a nutrient/dietary supplement and, for the green salt, as an anticaking agent for sodium chloride.
after.fact_1_copy: A complex of iron with citrate and ammonium, not simply iron metal or plain citric acid.
after.fact_2_copy: Used as an iron nutrient/dietary supplement and, in some forms, as an anticaking agent for salt.

name: Polysorbate 20 or Polyoxyethylene (20) sorbitan monolaurate
unresolved_question: Can fatty-acid feedstock be pinned to plant vs animal for Polysorbate 20?

sources.what: Definition uses edible commercial lauric acid; does not pin botanical vs animal origin.
USP notes fatty acids may be of vegetable, animal, or synthetic origin.

verified_facts: Origin is indeterminate from the additive code/specification alone.
Existing fact_2 hedge (plant or animal) is consistent with primary specs.
unsupported_possibilities: Declaring vegan/plant-only or animal-only from the E-number.
notes: Keep fail-closed hedge. No wording change required.

before.tile_summary: Polysorbate 20 is an emulsifier made from sorbitol-derived material, polyoxyethylene chains and lauric acid.
before.expanded_summary: Polysorbate 20 is an emulsifier made from sorbitol-derived material, polyoxyethylene chains and lauric acid. Its molecular design gives it both water-friendly and fat-friendly parts.
before.fact_1_copy: Helps oils, fats and water stay mixed and can stabilise foams or dispersions.
before.fact_2_copy: The fatty-acid feedstock may come from plant or animal fats, while the final emulsifier is chemically processed.

after.tile_summary: Polysorbate 20 is an emulsifier made from sorbitol-derived material, polyoxyethylene chains and lauric acid.
after.expanded_summary: Polysorbate 20 is an emulsifier made from sorbitol-derived material, polyoxyethylene chains and lauric acid. Its molecular design gives it both water-friendly and fat-friendly parts.
after.fact_1_copy: Helps oils, fats and water stay mixed and can stabilise foams or dispersions.
after.fact_2_copy: The fatty-acid feedstock may come from plant or animal fats, while the final emulsifier is chemically processed.

sources.what: Existing source_preparation_copy already states fatty-acid sources can be plant or animal.

before.expanded_summary: Diacetyltartaric and fatty acid esters of glycerol are emulsifiers made by adding diacetyltartaric acid-derived groups to mono- and diglyceride-type fat molecules. The modification changes how the molecules interact with dough, fat and water.

before.expanded_summary: L-cysteine hydrochloride is a salt of L-cysteine, a sulphur-containing amino acid found naturally in proteins. In food processing it is particularly known for changing dough properties.

Schedule 8 lists Octafluorocyclobutane (946).

before.tile_summary: Octafluorocyclobutane is a manufactured gas whose molecules contain only carbon and fluorine.
before.expanded_summary: Octafluorocyclobutane is a manufactured gas whose molecules contain only carbon and fluorine. Its name describes a ring of four carbon atoms (cyclobutane) with eight fluorine atoms attached.

before.fact_2_copy: Used for its gas/pressure properties rather than as a conventional solid or liquid ingredient.

name: Aspartame-acesulphame salt
unresolved_question: Can phenylalanine/PKU relevance be stated for aspartame-acesulphame salt?

sources.what: Mandatory advisory statement for foods containing aspartame or aspartame-acesulphame salt: the food contains phenylalanine.

verified_facts: 962 contains aspartame-derived material.
AU/NZ Code requires phenylalanine advisory for foods containing aspartame-acesulphame salt.
unsupported_possibilities: Clinical PKU advice beyond the mandated advisory statement.

before.tile_summary: Aspartame-acesulphame salt is a crystalline compound containing the two sweeteners aspartame and acesulphame in a fixed salt-like combination.
before.expanded_summary: Aspartame-acesulphame salt is a crystalline compound containing the two sweeteners aspartame and acesulphame in a fixed salt-like combination.
before.fact_1_copy: Two established high-intensity sweetener components in one ingredient.
before.fact_2_copy: Provides a blended sweetness profile without adding the two sweeteners separately.
before.fact_3_copy: The ingredient contains aspartame-derived material as well as acesulphame.

after.tile_summary: Aspartame-acesulphame salt is a crystalline compound containing the two sweeteners aspartame and acesulphame in a fixed salt-like combination.
after.expanded_summary: Aspartame-acesulphame salt is a crystalline compound containing the two sweeteners aspartame and acesulphame in a fixed salt-like combination. It provides a blended sweetness profile without adding the two sweeteners separately. Because it contains aspartame-derived material, foods that contain it require a phenylalanine advisory statement under the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code.
after.fact_1_copy: Two established high-intensity sweetener components in one ingredient.
after.fact_2_copy: Provides a blended sweetness profile without adding the two sweeteners separately.
